design.item: journals-home: get-view-data {:journals? true} returns every journal (7.2 s worker block at 10k)
design.summary: The journals home asks the worker for the ids of all journals. get-latest-journals turns the whole :block/journal-day AVET slice into a vector and does a d/entity plus journal? check on every journal, which is 10 000 restores from SQLite at 10k. The UI already renders a virtualized list and never reads :count, so it does not need all ids. Fix: make get-latest-journals walk the index backwards lazily from today, have get-view-data return the first N ids plus :more?, and have the journals component grow N through react-virtuoso's endReached. Worker work then depends on how far the user has scrolled, not on graph size.

DATASCRIPT FACTS (checked)

changes.change:
Replace the eager `vec` + `rseq` with a lazy backwards index walk that starts at today. Same output order as today (journal-day descending, then entity id descending), and future days are no longer scanned at all:
```clojure
(defn get-latest-journals
  "Journal page entities, newest first, journal-day <= today. Lazy: walks the
   :block/journal-day AVET index backwards from today; callers bound the work
   with take/first."
  [db]
  (let [today (date-time-util/date->int (js/Date.))]
    (->> (d/rseek-datoms db :avet :block/journal-day today)
         (take-while #(= :block/journal-day (:a %)))
         (keep (fn [d]
                 (let [e (d/entity db (:e d))]
                   (when (and (common-entity-util/journal? e) (:db/id e))
                     e)))))))
```
- The upper bound is (emax, :block/journal-day, today, txmax), so every entity on today's day is included.
- The `take-while` is required because the rslice lower bound has no attribute.
- The call is nil-safe on an empty db, since `rslice` uses `some->`.
- It also works on a FilteredDB (lazy `filter`), which `(rseq (d/index-range ...))` would not.
- model.cljs:363, container.cljs:175 and validate.cljs:71 become O(1) with no change on their side.

Bound the result with an optional `:limit`. Read it as `(:limit opts)` so it cannot clash with the destructured keys, and default it so no caller can ask for everything by accident. Take one extra id to compute `:more?`, and drop `:count` (nothing reads it):
```clojure
journals?
(let [limit (or (:limit opts) 10)
      ids   (into [] (comp (map :db/id) (take (inc limit)))
                  (ldb/get-latest-journals db))
      more? (> (count ids) limit)]
  {:data  (if more? (pop ids) ids)
   :more? more?})
```
Optional ADR-003 candidate budget: also stop after about `(* 4 (inc limit))` scanned datoms and return `:more? true`. That covers the pathological case of many `:block/journal-day` datoms on entities that fail `journal?`. File graphs set journal-day only on journal pages (block.cljs:356-360), so this is belt and braces.

Keep the `react/q` key `[:frontend.worker.react/journals]` unchanged so the DB-graph refresh and `re-render-root!` keep working. Make the limit component state that the cached `query-fn` reads when it runs, and grow it on endReached:
```clojure
(def ^:private journals-page-size 10)

(defn- sub-journals
  [*limit]
  (when-let [repo (state/get-current-repo)]
    (some-> (react/q repo [:frontend.worker.react/journals]
                     {:query-fn (fn [_]
                                  ;; deref at run time: refresh-affected-queries! re-runs this cached fn
                                  (p/let [{:keys [data more?]} (views/<load-view-data nil {:journals? true :limit @*limit})]
                                    {:ids (vec (remove nil? data)) :more? more?}))}
                     nil)
            util/react)))

(rum/defcs all-journals < rum/reactive db-mixins/query
  (rum/local journals-page-size ::limit)
  [state]
  (let [*limit (::limit state)
        {:keys [ids more?]} (sub-journals *limit)]
    (when (seq ids)
      [:div#journals
       (ui/virtualized-list
        {:custom-scroll-parent (util/app-scroll-container-node)
         :increase-viewport-by {:top 100 :bottom 100}
         :compute-item-key (fn [idx] (str "journal-" (util/nth-safe ids idx)))
         :total-count (count ids)
         :end-reached (fn [_idx]
                        ;; grow once per loaded page; ignore repeats while a fetch is in flight
                        (when (and more? (>= (count ids) @*limit))
                          (swap! *limit + journals-page-size)
                          (react/refresh-affected-queries! (state/get-current-repo)
                                                           [[:frontend.worker.react/journals]]
                                                           :skip-kv-custom-keys? true)))
         :item-content (fn [idx]
                         (let [id (util/nth-safe ids idx)
                               last? (and (not more?) (= (inc idx) (count ids)))]
                           (journal-cp id last?)))})])))
```
Notes:
- Callers (`(journal/all-journals)` in container.cljs:185 and mobile app.cljs:32, route `:view` in routes.cljs:78) pass no user args, so `defcs [state]` keeps the arity.
- `refresh-affected-queries!` is public (react.cljs:173). `:skip-kv-custom-keys? true` stops every scroll step from also re-running all `:custom` default queries ("Scheduled and Deadline").
- After `clear-query-state!`, the next render builds a new query whose `query-fn` closes over the same `rum/local` atom (`request-render` does not unmount), so the depth the user has loaded survives refreshes.
- On unmount, `remove-query-component!` calls `remove-q!` (react.cljs:63-66,76-86). A return to home starts at one page again.

design.ui_contract_risks:
- **journal.cljs sub-journals / all-journals** (the only reader of the journals branch):
  - The result shape changes from a seq of ids to `{:ids :more?}`, but only inside this component.
  - `(when (seq ids))` keeps today's empty behaviour.
  - Item keys stay "journal-<id>", so already rendered items are not remounted when the list grows.
- **Nothing reads `:count`:** views.cljs load-view-data-aux (2146-2150) destructures only data/ref-pages-count/ref-matched-children-ids/properties, and it is not used for journals.
- **Same component in three places:** home (container.cljs:174-185), `:all-journals` (routes.cljs:76-78) and mobile (app.cljs:29-32) all behave the same. Mobile is DB-graph only, and its `:journals?` mobile-length-limit in page.cljs:184 is unaffected.
- **DB-graph refresh:** the `[::journals]` affected key (worker/react.cljs:47-51,90-91) still matches the unchanged key and re-runs `query-fn` with the current limit.
- **File-graph refresh:** `re-render-root!` (ui.cljs:82-93; called from page.cljs:~349 and pipeline.cljs:56-59) clears the cache and re-queries with the component's current limit. It is now bounded, so the per-file-change re-query stops being a 7 s stall.
- **Day rollover:** "today" is computed in the worker at call time. `create-today-journal!` then `re-render-root!` puts the new day on top.
- **Future-dated journal pages:** still excluded; the rseek starts at today.
- **Order:** identical to today (v descending, e descending), including several entities on the same day. rseek covers the whole today bucket (emax).
- **Other `get-latest-journals` callers** only use `first`/`take` (model.cljs:363, validate.cljs:71, container.cljs:175). Both old and new return a lazy seq, so they behave the same, just cheaper.
- **`journal-last-item`:** the marker now goes on the last loaded item only when `(not more?)`. I did not check what that CSS does (it may add a bottom margin or min-height). Check it visually; if it is what makes the page scrollable, keep the old `last?` rule.
- **endReached timing:** react-virtuoso fires endReached when the last item is rendered, including the overscan set by `increase-viewport-by`, and again when totalCount changes. That should also chain loads when the first page does not fill the viewport. This is Virtuoso's documented behaviour, not verified in this app; see verification.
- **Race between fetches:** a tx-triggered re-query and a scroll-triggered one each read `@*limit` when they run. A response with a smaller limit could land after a larger one and briefly shorten the list. The guard `(>= (count ids) @*limit)` then lets endReached fire again, so it heals itself. The fuller version's generation token removes the race.
- **Existing blank flash:** after `clear-query-state!` the new result atom starts nil, so the list blanks until the worker answers. This already happens today, and it is now shorter.
- **react/q sharing:** the key is global per repo. Two mounted `all-journals` instances would share the first instance's `query-fn`/limit. That cannot happen today (one route at a time).
design.expected_gain:
`get-view-data {:journals? true}` at 10k: 7236 ms on reopen and 5756 ms after first open (15 808 restores) should drop to O(limit):
- one root-to-leaf path in the AVET tree at today (depth 3-4, a few restores),
- 11 datoms, usually within one or two leaves,
- 11 `d/entity` + `:block/type` lookups (at most about 11 EAVT leaf restores).

That is roughly 10-30 restores, so I expect under 50 ms, below the thread-api perf-log threshold, at g-real and g-10k alike. g-real's 102 ms also drops.

Knock-on gains:
- The re-query that `re-render-root!` triggers after every from-disk change and after today's journal is created becomes bounded too.
- `get-latest-journals` on the UI thread (container.cljs:175, on every home render) and in validate.cljs:71 goes from O(journals) to O(1).

What stays linear:
- Scrolling back N journals costs O(N) per re-query, because the smallest version re-fetches the top N instead of appending. That scales with how deep the user has scrolled, not with graph size.
- Outside this item and unchanged: each rendered journal's `page-cp` block load (`get-block-and-children` counts all children, initial_data.cljs:220-222), the "Scheduled and Deadline" `thread-api/q`, `get-initial-data` (8.4 s at 10k) and the 5 s boot parse of main.js.

Fuller ADR-003 version (if the smallest change is not enough):
- **Request:** `{:journals? true :limit n :after [journal-day e] :generation g}`.
- **Walk:** the worker continues from `(d/rseek-datoms db :avet :block/journal-day day e)` with a full-key cursor, skipping the cursor datom itself so days shared by several entities are handled.
- **Response:** `{:data ids :cursor [v e] :more? :generation g' :provenance {:store :datascript :reconcile-state …}}`, built under a candidate budget (datoms scanned) and a time budget.
- **Generation mismatch:** the worker rejects a stale cursor and the UI restarts from the top, never mixing pages from different generations. The generation could be the db's max-tx or a counter the worker bumps per transaction (not verified in the fork).
- **UI:** appends pages instead of re-fetching the top N. On a change, it reloads the first page and restarts the cursor chain.
- **Count:** none needed; the list only uses `:more?`.
- **Refresh:** also emit `[::journals]` when a tx touches `:block/journal-day`, a one-line change in worker/react.cljs:47-51, so file graphs refresh without `re-render-root!`.

design.open_questions:
1. Page size: 10 is my assumption. Journal items render whole pages, so 5-10 is probably enough. The 0.10-era file-graph UI started with about 3 and loaded more on scroll, from memory and not verified in this tree.
2. What the `journal-last-item` CSS does. Check before moving the marker to the last item only when `(not more?)`.
3. react-virtuoso 4.12.5 endReached with `customScrollParent`: I expect it to fire on the initial render when content is shorter than the viewport, but this is not verified in this app.
4. Whether to also cap `:limit` in the worker (e.g. 2000) as an ADR budget. Capping would stop infinite scroll at the cap unless the cursor version is built.
5. File graphs never get the `[::journals]` refresh key (worker/react.cljs:47-51 checks for the Journal class tag, which file graphs lack). Journal pages created in-app without a disk sync or root re-render therefore do not appear until the next `re-render-root!`. This predates the change and the change does not fix it. The one-line fix (also trigger on `:block/journal-day` datoms) is cheap now that the query is bounded, but it changes refresh frequency, so I left it out of the smallest change.
6. If the cursor version is built, what the generation token should be: db max-tx, or a counter the worker bumps per transaction. Not checked in the fork.

critique.breakages:
The core worker change looks correct. I found no existing caller it breaks:
- The rseek bounds are right. `components->pattern` for :avet (db.cljc:1144-1148) gives the upper bound (emax, :block/journal-day, today, txmax).
- `cmp-datoms-avet` (db.cljc:514-519) uses the nil-safe `cmp`/`value-cmp`, so the lower bound (e0 nil nil tx0) sorts before every datom. The walk therefore does run into earlier attributes, and the `take-while` is needed.
- Reverse traversal restores lazily through storage: `-prev-path` and `-rpath` call `child ... (.-storage set)` at pss:762-800.
- The order matches today's.
- The only consumer of the journals branch is journal.cljs:26. The e2e tests only call `goto-journals` and count nothing.

Concrete problems in the UI part:
1. **The optional candidate budget deadlocks infinite scroll.** Suppose the worker stops early and returns fewer than `limit` ids with `:more? true`. The endReached guard `(>= (count ids) @*limit)` is then false forever. Virtuoso's endReached is deduplicated (index.mjs:1557-1566, `V(last originalIndex === totalCount-1)` then `Y(se)`), so it will not fire again for the same totalCount either. The list stops growing until remount. The guard must key on an in-flight flag or on `more?` plus a request token, not on count >= limit.
2. **A failed fetch sticks the same way.** If `<load-view-data` rejects, count stays below the limit, the guard blocks, and endReached is deduplicated. The list only recovers on remount or `re-render-root!`.
3. **`:limit` has no cap, so depth becomes the new graph-size cost.** Every `re-render-root!` re-fetches the top N. That fires once per from-disk sync (pipeline.cljs:56-59), and an external sync or git pull of many files fires it in bursts, while the user is scrolled deep. At N in the thousands this brings back multi-second stalls. It also violates ADR point 2 (budgets per batch).
4. **The lazy seq now reaches further.** `get-latest-journals` is lazy all the way into the AVET walk; before, the `vec` realized it. The ADR (§3) notes old db values are not durable snapshots because node addresses are reused. Today's worker callers realize it right away: view with `into`, validate with `first`. The docstring should say "realize within the same synchronous call" so a future caller does not hold it across a transact.

Non-issues:
- `journal-last-item` is only `@apply border-none` (journal.css:16-17). Open question 2 is moot.
- Arity and caching of `query-fn`: `execute-query!` calls `(query-fn db nil)`, the same as today.
critique.gain_doubts:
The gain is real for the call measured.
- Today, 100% of `get-view-data` `{:journals? true}` time is the `vec` over `get-latest-journals` plus about 10k `d/entity`/`:block/type` restores. The new walk costs two root-to-leaf paths in `-slice` (pss:1127-1131; the lower-bound seek goes to the leftmost AVET leaf, which is harmless), about 11 datoms, and at most one extra leaf because of the eager `(rest s)` in keep/take-while. That is tens of restores.
- It removes the stall at the default depth only. Cost is O(scroll depth) per scroll step and per `re-render-root!`, so a deep scroll plus a burst of disk syncs brings stalls back.
- It does nothing for the per-journal page-cp/refs loads, `get-initial-data` (8.4 s), the filtered views, or `<get-files` on every search. Home-page reopen at 10k is still dominated by the 8.4 s `get-initial-data`.
critique.required_changes:
1. **Replace the endReached guard.** Use a request/generation token or an in-flight flag, and allow loading whenever `more?` is true after the response lands. Never compare count to limit, because that deadlocks with any worker budget and with fetch failures.
2. **Cap and budget in the worker, per ADR-003 point 2.** Cap `:limit` (for example 200 per batch), add the candidate/time budget, and return `:more?` truthfully. If deep scroll must stay cheap, build the cursor-append version (full-key `[journal-day e]` cursor, skip the cursor datom). Re-fetching the top N does not scale with depth.
3. **Carry generation and provenance, per ADR-003 points 3-4.** Put at least a generation (for example the worker's per-tx counter, or max-tx) and `{:store :datascript}` in the response. Have the UI drop responses whose token is older than the latest request. This also fixes the stale-response race the proposal acknowledges.
4. **Document the laziness contract** in `get-latest-journals`: callers inside the worker must realize the seq synchronously.
5. **Fix the load-view-data-aux citation** (views.cljs:2197 and about 2223).
6. **Tests.** Add a case for "budget stops early with `:more? true` and the UI keeps loading", and one for a stale response arriving after a newer one.

design.item: file-search: bound the per-query work of search.cljs file-search (and the other callers of db-async/<get-files)
design.summary: Every search keystroke (cmdk :files group, debounced to 200 ms) and every plugin-API search runs db-async/<get-files. That call is a worker thread-api/q which pulls [:file/path :file/last-modified-at] for every file entity, only for file-search to throw away all md/org paths. Measured cost: 5.5–6.2 s of blocked worker per query at 10k. Fix: add a worker endpoint that reads :file/path straight from the AVET index (no pull, so no EAVT and no :file/content restores). It returns a cached vector of non-mldoc paths per repo. A DataScript listener drops that cache only when a non-mldoc :file/path datom is added or retracted, or the conn is reset or replaced. file-search keeps its UI-side filter and fuzzy logic unchanged. The startup watcher uses the same endpoint in all-paths mode.
design.current_behavior:
CALLERS OF file-search (src/main/frontend/search.cljs:29-43)
- frontend/handler/search.cljs:34-35, `search`: `(p/let [blocks (search/block-search ...) files (search/file-search q)] ...)`, limit 3. Its only caller is the plugin API `search` in logseq/api.cljs:181-184.
- frontend/components/cmdk/core.cljs:332-352, `(defmethod load-results :files ...)` calls `(search/file-search @!input 99)`. It then drops .edn paths under whiteboards/ and assets/, logseq/version-files, and the three metadata .edn files (lines ~337-345).
- It is triggered by `load-results :default` (cmdk/core.cljs:416-431, `:files` at line 428) on every input change when the input is non-empty and no filter group is set. The input is debounced to 200 ms (cmdk/core.cljs:861-868). It also runs for the "Search only files" filter (cmdk/core.cljs:68).
- There are no other callers. mobile/ does not call it.

WHAT file-search DOES
- It computes mldoc-exts = #{"org" "markdown" "md"} (logseq/common/config.cljs:84-85).
- It calls `(db-async/<get-files repo)`, takes `(map first)` to get the paths, and removes any path whose `(util/get-file-ext file)` is in mldoc-exts.
- util/get-file-ext is frontend/util.cljc:1011-1016: a string that contains ".", and lower-cased `common-util/path->file-ext`. path->file-ext is logseq/common/util.cljs:186-189.
- Finally it runs `(fuzzy/fuzzy-search files q :limit limit)` (frontend/common/search_fuzzy.cljs:80-90). That scores every item and does a stable sort-by score.

CALLERS OF <get-files (db/async.cljs:30-37)
- The function itself: `(<q graph {:transact-db? false} '[:find [(pull ?file [:file/path :file/last-modified-at]) ...] :where [?file :file/path ?path]])`, then `reverse`, mapped to `[path (or mtime 0)]`.
- With :transact-db? false, the UI-local cache branch of <q, `(and async-requested? transact-db?)` in db/async/util.cljs <q, is never taken. Every call goes to `:thread-api/q` (db_worker.cljs:492-495), which is a synchronous `d/q` over the whole db.
- Callers: search.cljs:37 (above); components/file.cljs:32-37 (the `files-all` "All files" page, which needs path and mtime); fs/watcher_handler.cljs:142-143 (`load-graph-files!`, which keeps only `(map first ...)` and so discards the mtime).
- db/model.cljs:38 `get-files-full` and fs.cljs:188 `get-files` are different functions.

WHY THE QUERY IS SO EXPENSIVE (code path verified; the time split is not measured)
- `[?file :file/path ?path]` is an AEVT slice (datascript db.cljc, `-search` case `_ a _ _`). The pull then reads each file entity's EAVT datoms.
- File entities carry `:file/content` (file_based/schema.cljs:95-99; set on the file entity by parse-file-data, graph_parser.cljs:83-85).
- They also get entity ids interleaved with the pages and blocks of the same parse transaction, so pulling 10k files restores about one content-bearing EAVT leaf per file. Leaves hold 16–32 datoms (persistent-sorted-set 0.1.2, max-len 32).
- Restored nodes sit behind a WeakRef and get evicted, so every search pays this again. That fits 6185 ms followed by 5524 ms.
- On top of that, the result is transit-written as 10k maps.
- Because the worker is serial, each debounced keystroke queues about 6 s of q in front of `search-blocks`. That plausibly explains "hits never appeared within 30 s" (an inference).

IS THE WATCHER CALL ON EVERY STARTUP? Yes.
- It runs on every app start of a local file graph: handler.cljs:174-180 (the start sequence calls `restore-and-setup!`) → db/restore.cljs:38 publishes `:graph/restored` → events.cljs:260-265 publishes `:graph/ready` (skipped only on native iOS) → events.cljs:171-188 calls `(fs-watcher/load-graph-files! repo)` for file graphs when not publishing.
- It also runs on every graph switch (handler/repo.cljs:68-74, `restore-and-setup-repo!`) and after an import (components/imports.cljs:423).

WHAT THE WATCHER COSTS
1. One `<get-files`. This is the identical `thread-api/q` with identical arguments, so the same order of worker stall as a search (5.5–6.2 s at 10k, inferred). The LSPERF args string is the same for both callers, so one of the two measurements labelled "search" may actually be this startup call.
2. Then, after a 500 ms delay, it runs `p/all` over every file on disk (watcher_handler.cljs ~183-197). Per file it does:
   - `fs/stat` and `fs/read-file` over IPC;
   - `db/file-exists?` on the UI db (db/model.cljs:32-36). That works only because get-initial-data ships every file entity's datoms to the UI (initial_data.cljs:58-61, `get-all-files`);
   - `handle-changed!` → `db-async/<get-file` (db/async.cljs:194-198) → `<pull [:file/path path]` with selector `[*]` → a worker `d/pull`. That restores the content-bearing leaf, ships the whole content to the UI, and `d/transact!`s it into the UI db (db/async/util.cljs `<pull`);
   - finally `(= content db-content)`, which in an unchanged graph ends in a no-op.
3. At 10k that adds up to about 10k IPC reads (41 MB), about 10k worker pulls (~3 s of restores at the measured average of 5531 ms / 18 392 restores ≈ 0.3 ms per restore; an estimate), and 41 MB of content shipped worker→UI.
This design fixes step 1. Step 2 stays linear; it is ADR-003 plan step 2 (mtime+size reconcile).

changes.change:
Reads :file/path from AVET only, plus a per-repo cache of non-mldoc paths. Requires only clojure.string, datascript.core, logseq.common.config and logseq.common.util. No worker ns requires frontend.util (grep), so the predicate re-expresses util/get-file-ext with the same common-util fn it delegates to.

(def ^:private mldoc-exts (set (map name common-config/mldoc-support-formats)))
(defn mldoc-path? [path]   ; == (mldoc-exts (util/get-file-ext path)), util.cljc:1011-1016
  (boolean (and (string? path) (string/includes? path ".")
                (contains? mldoc-exts (some-> (common-util/path->file-ext path) string/lower-case)))))
(defn all-paths [db] (mapv :v (d/datoms db :avet :file/path)))
(defonce ^:private *non-mldoc (atom {}))            ; repo -> {:conn conn :paths [..]}
(defn forget! [repo] (swap! *non-mldoc dissoc repo))
(defn- touches-non-mldoc-path? [tx-data]
  (some #(and (= :file/path (:a %)) (not (mldoc-path? (:v %)))) tx-data))
(defn non-mldoc-paths [repo conn]
  (let [{c :conn paths :paths} (get @*non-mldoc repo)]
    (if (identical? c conn)
      paths
      (let [paths (into [] (comp (map :v) (remove mldoc-path?)) (d/datoms @conn :avet :file/path))]
        (d/listen! conn ::non-mldoc-paths
                   (fn [{:keys [tx-data tx-meta]}]
                     (when (or (:reset-conn! tx-meta) (touches-non-mldoc-path? tx-data))
                       (forget! repo))))
        (swap! *non-mldoc assoc repo {:conn conn :paths paths})
        paths))))

Why this is safe:
- `(d/datoms db :avet :file/path)` is valid: :file/path is :db.unique/identity, which implies :db/index (datascript db.cljc:874). initial_data.cljs:60 already calls it unconditionally for every graph type.
- Build, then listen!, is synchronous in the single-threaded worker, so no transaction can slip in between.
- It uses a raw d/listen! under its own key, not a listen-db-changes defmethod. Raw listeners fire on every transact, including inside batch-tx mode, whereas the defmethod handlers are deferred to batch exit (db_listener.cljs:92-124). listen-db-changes! unlistens only its own key (db_listener.cljs:78).
- md/org adds, removes and renames never invalidate, because the non-mldoc set is unaffected by them.

(def-thread-api :thread-api/get-file-paths

Fuller version: a paginated table fed by a cursor over `d/seek-datoms :avet :file/path`, with the mtime looked up only for the current page.

Assert:

(2) Adding or retracting a .md file keeps the same vector (identical?).
(3) Adding, retracting, or renaming via `{:db/id e :file/path new}` a non-mldoc path produces a rebuilt vector with the change.

design.expected_gain:
SEARCH
- Today: 5.5–6.2 s of blocked worker per file-search at 10k (measured twice), repeated on every debounced cmdk keystroke and every plugin search. Each one also delays the queued search-blocks call behind it.
- After: a steady-state call returns a cached vector of the non-mldoc paths, and the UI fuzzy-scores those. That is tens of paths (logseq/config.edn, custom.css, whiteboards/*.edn), sub-millisecond (estimate), and independent of journal and page count.
- One-time cost per worker session (at the first search), and again only after a non-mldoc file is added, removed or renamed: an AVET walk over :file/path. At 10k that is about 310–625 leaf restores (leaf size 16–32), roughly 0.1–0.2 s at the measured ~0.3 ms per restore (estimate). It never touches EAVT or :file/content.

STARTUP WATCHER
- The `<get-files` q, probably the same ~5.5–6 s (inferred, identical query), becomes the same AVET walk without the filter: est. 0.1–0.2 s plus ~400 KB of transit.

WHAT STAYS LINEAR
- The one-time AVET walk: O(files) with a small constant.
- The fuzzy scoring over non-mldoc paths, which grows with the number of whiteboards and css/edn files, not with the number of notes.
- The rest of load-graph-files!: stat plus read of every disk file over IPC, a full-content <get-file pull per file into the UI db, and a string compare.
- The files-all page.

FULLER ADR-003 VERSION
(a) `:thread-api/search-files {:q :limit}` doing the fuzzy match in the worker. It returns at most `limit` hits plus `{:generation g}`, with g bumped by the same listener.
(b) Maintain the non-mldoc set incrementally (conj/disj from tx-data) and persist it, or build it with a budgeted, resumable cursor walk (`d/seek-datoms :avet :file/path`) that reports "index incomplete" until done. Then nothing is O(files) even once per session.
(c) Replace the startup reconcile with a paged cursor walk returning `[path mtime size]` per page, compare against fs/stat, and read only changed files. Run it in the background with a visible generation (ADR plan step 2).
(d) A paginated files-all page.

design.open_questions:
1. Attribution. The two 10k measurements labelled "q pull all files on every search" (6185 and 5524 ms) are the same thread-api/q with the same args as the startup `load-graph-files!` call, and the LSPERF args string cannot tell them apart. One of them may be the startup call. Tagging the call site or re-measuring would settle it.

2. The empty blocks_fts at 10k is a separate bug. After this fix search is fast, but it still finds only page titles until that is fixed.

3. Is the tie-order change acceptable (unspecified hash order becomes deterministic path order)? My assumption: yes, since the old order carried no contract.

4. Alternative I did not choose: file-search could read `(d/datoms ui-db :avet :file/path)` directly in the UI. The UI db already holds every file entity (initial_data.cljs:58-61), and load-graph-files! already relies on that through db/file-exists? (db/model.cljs:32-36). That costs no worker time, but it is still O(files) per keystroke on the UI thread. Make it lazy. `vec` on the index slice currently realizes every journal. Replace with:
(->> (d/rseek-datoms db :avet :block/journal-day (inc today))
     (take-while #(= :block/journal-day (:a %)))
     (filter #(<= (:v %) today))
     (keep (fn [d] (let [e (d/entity db (:e d))] (when (and (common-entity-util/journal? e) (:db/id e)) e)))))
`d/rseek-datoms` exists in the pinned fork (~/.gitlibs/libs/datascript/datascript/3971e2d…/src/datascript/core.cljc:404). design.ui_contract_risks:
The UI DataScript copy already acts as a lazy cache for blocks (`:block.temp/load-status`, `<get-block` in async.cljs:85-137). This change extends that contract to pages and files. Every consumer that assumed completeness, and how the design keeps it working:

1. **Save path (typing, highest risk).** `alter-files` and `write-file-aux!` took old content from the UI db, and `fs/node` falls back to `""` and then writes a backup (node.cljs:40-46).
   - Kept working by: the worker ships `:old-contents` with `:write-files`, and write-file-aux! falls back to `<get-file`.
   - Test: count the files in logseq/bak before and after a typing session on journals and linked references. It must not grow.
2. **Config and theme at first paint.** `restore-repo-config!` and `add-style-if-exists!` read config.edn and custom.css synchronously.
   - Kept working by: both files are in the boot set.
   - custom.js stays fs-read for file graphs.
3. **Startup reconcile and deletes.**
   - add/change typing is benign even when wrong (handle-changed! compares against the worker's content, watcher_handler.cljs:77-89), but the design uses the `<get-files` set anyway.
   - Deleted-file-to-page and `<delete!` by name would silently no-op. Fixed by the worker lookup and delete-by-uuid.
   - Residual: the rest of `<delete!` after common/page.cljs:172 was not read. Verify that it tolerates a missing UI entity; `d/entity` on an unresolved lookup ref returns nil, so home-page? becomes false.
4. **Today journal.** Covered by the boot set and the async re-check. The worker already blocks duplicate creation.
5. **Sidebar.**
   - Favorites and recent: in the boot set.
   - Later favorites from a hand-edited config.edn: async hydrate.
   - Recent ids persisted from a different graph generation are skipped when they have no `:block/name`.
6. **Page references and titles.**
   - page-cp-inner and page-reference fall back to `<get-block` when the page is not loaded. This costs one worker call per distinct unloaded referenced page on first render; it is not graph-proportional.
   - The truthy-empty-entity issue is fixed by checking `:block/uuid`.
   - Blocks loaded through get-block-and-children carry their refs and page as nested maps (entity->map, initial_data.cljs:136-164), so most refs arrive already loaded.
7. **Namespace hierarchy, query builder, and the plugin `get_pages_from_namespace` / tree.** Would be silently partial; moved to the worker.
8. **Editor "New page" hint and property-key links.** Cosmetic; fixed as described.
9. **Alias redirect.** `get-redirect-page-name` (model.cljs:334-356) resolves aliases on the UI db, so an alias whose page is not loaded would not redirect to its source page. Not fixed here; must be tested (navigate by alias after reopen) and, if needed, resolved through `<get-block` first.
10. **`<q` result cache** (async/util.cljs:31-40). Queries answered from the UI db on repeat can become incomplete. The audit step above covers it.
11. **Unaffected (verified worker-backed):**
    - search
    - all pages and journals list (get-view-data)
    - graph view
    - custom `{{query}}`
    - plugin `get_page` / `get_all_pages`
    - page open
    - `<get-file` / `<get-files`
12. **Pipeline.** Worker tx-data applied by eid (pipeline.cljs:51-72) can create partial page or file entities in the UI db. Name lookups ignore entities without `:block/name`, `db/page?` filters them, and the page-cp change handles id lookups. Retractions of absent datoms are no-ops.
13. **DB-graph code path** is unchanged. The `:file-graph-import?` full-datom path (db_worker.cljs:625-627) is unchanged. Mobile/desktop parity holds: everything stays in the worker.

**get-initial-data** at g-10k: 93 007 datoms, 18 375 restores and 8465 ms sync become a boot set that does not depend on graph size:
- 3 files, at most 3 journals, F favorites, at most 20 recent pages, at most 15 recently updated pages;

1. TYPING CORRUPTS PAGE IDENTITY. This is the highest-risk path and the design does not mention it.
   - The file-graph save runs on the UI thread: editor.cljs:262-275 → file_based/editor.cljs wrap-parse-block (84-140) → format/block.cljs parse-block → gp-block/extract-blocks with `:db (db/get-db repo)`, the UI db (format/block.cljs:27).
   - page-name-string->map (graph_parser/block.cljs:317-345) reuses an existing page's :block/uuid and :block/title only if `ldb/get-page db name` finds the page in that db. Otherwise it creates a random uuid (non-journal pages) and keeps the typed casing.
   - The ref maps reach the worker unchanged. outliner core -save does `(swap! *txs-state conj (dissoc m :db/other-tx))` (core.cljs:387-389). file-rebuild-block-refs (144-180) is not called from -save.

   - Journal refs are safe: their uuids are deterministic (gen-uuid :journal-page-uuid).
   - Today this cannot happen, because every page is in the UI db.
   - Related: remove-non-existed-refs! (file_based/editor.cljs:34-40) drops `[:block/uuid x]` refs that are absent from the UI db.

TESTS. src/test/frontend/db/file_based/model_test.cljs:9-32 calls the sync get-namespace-pages and get-page-namespace-routes, so the async conversion must keep the sync fns or update the tests. deps/db/test/.../initial_data_test.cljs:29-44 (config.edn content in initial data) still passes. restore-initial-data (46-60) is a DB graph and is unaffected.

critique.notes:
The direction matches ADR-003: a bounded boot set, with the worker as the complete source. The individual mechanics are fine:
- The lazy get-latest-journals via rseek-datoms is correct. rseek-datoms exists in the fork at core.cljc:404; take-while plus the <= filter make start inclusivity irrelevant. Its callers (model.cljs:360-363, container.cljs:175, validate.cljs:71, view.cljs:439) all tolerate a lazy seq.
- page-cp-inner's truthy empty entity is real: db.cljs:330-331 `(d/entity db id)` on a number.
- create-or-open-db (db_worker.cljs:486-490) passes opts to start-db!; that extra keys are ignored there was not verified.
- journal-cp → page-cp {:db/id} → page-aux already calls <get-block (components/page.cljs:759-765), so the journals list survives an empty boot set.
The real problem is the silent completeness assumptions on the write path (the parser resolves refs against the UI db) and the query path (the query DSL). The design's consumer list misses both. Its gain estimate also ignores load-graph-files!, which re-pulls every file into the UI at each reopen. Merge the design once findings 1-3 are fixed and the gain is re-baselined.

design.item: First open / re-index: per-file SQLite store and per-file root re-render during the bulk parse loop
design.summary: Each file's reset-file transact writes to SQLite synchronously in the worker, and each file's sync makes the UI call re-render-root!. A finding that changes the design: for file graphs `:skip-store?` has no effect at all. The DataScript fork's `-transact!` removes it before building the tx report, so adding it at graph_parser.cljs:187 would change nothing. Proposal: thread a `:bulk-load?` flag from the parse loop to the worker. In `ldb/transact-sync`, honour it for file graphs by deferring the store, as the DB-graph branch already does. Write checkpoints from the worker once the unsaved datoms pass a size budget, and add an explicit `:thread-api/flush-storage` call at the end of parsing, before after-parse. The UI pipeline skips re-render-root! for bulk syncs; after-parse's existing single re-render (after the flush) replaces them. Watcher and external edits keep storing and re-rendering on every change.
design.current_behavior:
PARSE LOOP (UI): parse-files-and-create-default-files-inner! (src/main/frontend/handler/file_based/repo.cljs:155-215) handles one file at a time. For each file, parse-and-load-file! (repo.cljs:91) calls file-handler/alter-file with {:from-disk? true :new-graph? ...}. alter-file (handler/file_based/file.cljs:139) builds a fixed opts map at file.cljs:154 ({:new-graph? :from-disk? :fs/event :ctime :mtime}, so extra keys are dropped) and calls reset-file! (file.cljs:36-40), which runs :thread-api/reset-file (db_worker.cljs:825-829), then file-reset/reset-file! (worker/file/reset.cljs; passes options through), then graph-parser/parse-file, which does `(ldb/transact! conn tx (select-keys options [:new-graph? :from-disk?]))` at deps/graph-parser/src/logseq/graph_parser.cljs:187. At the end the loop calls after-parse (repo.cljs:214 → 141-152), which already does one re-render-root! when re-render? is true (the default, repo.cljs:223), then pubs :graph/added (repo.cljs:147 → events.cljs:70-76: search rebuild, redirect-to-home!, watch-dir!).

WORKER TRANSACT: the worker never registers *transact-fn (it is registered only on the UI thread, persist_db/browser.cljs:153), so ldb/transact! (deps/db/src/logseq/db.cljs:177) goes to transact-sync (db.cljs:105). A file graph is not db-based, so it reaches `(d/transact! conn tx-data tx-meta)` (db.cljs:138). In the fork (~/.gitlibs/libs/datascript/datascript/3971e2d…/src/datascript/conn.cljc), -transact! does `tx-meta' (dissoc tx-meta :skip-store?)` (conn.cljc:104) before `with`, and `with` puts tx-meta' into the TxReport (conn.cljc:29). store-after-transact! (conn.cljc:111) checks `(get-in tx-report [:tx-meta :skip-store?])` (conn.cljc:90), which is therefore always nil. Result: for file graphs, EVERY transact stores, including UI transacts where thread-api/transact adds :skip-store? true (db_worker.cljs:603). Only the DB-graph branch of transact-sync (d/with with the original tx-meta, then dc/store-after-transact!, db.cljs:~110-127) honours it.

HOW DEFERRED (:skip-store?) TRANSACTS ARE PERSISTED, where the flag is honoured: store-after-transact! always conj's the tx datoms onto the conn's in-memory :tx-tail. Without skip: if the summed tail exceeds :branching-factor (default 512, core.cljc:165), it calls storage/store-impl! (storage.cljs:91). That writes every dirty node of eavt/aevt/avet, the root meta and an empty tail in one -store call, which is one SQLite transaction (upsert-addr-content!, db_worker.cljs:147-155, `.transaction`); then it resets :tx-tail [] and :db-last-stored. Otherwise store-tail (storage.cljs:141) re-writes the whole accumulated tail as one kvs row. With skip, only the conj happens. Nothing flushes it except the NEXT non-skip transact on the same conn, which writes the accumulated tail or, usually, a full store-impl!. There is no timer, no idle flush and no close-time flush: close-db-aux! (db_worker.cljs:256) only calls .close. `d/store`, `store-impl!` and `:tx-tail` appear nowhere in src/ or deps/ (grep); the only app call is dc/store-after-transact! at db.cljs:127. On restore, restore-impl (storage.cljs:144) replays root plus tail.

PER-FILE COST TODAY: every file calls store-tail, which transit-writes the whole pending tail (up to 512 datoms). Every few files a store-impl! re-serializes every dirty leaf (up to 512 datoms) and its ancestors in all three indexes. Attribute-clustered AEVT/AVET leaves are rewritten again and again across files.

UI SYNC: the listener sync-db-to-main-thread (worker/db_listener.cljs:19-44) broadcasts :sync-db-changes with the full tx-data and tx-meta (shared_service.cljs:359-366). The worker's invoke-hooks returns just {:tx-report} for from-disk?/new-graph? (worker/pipeline.cljs:512-518), so there are no affected-keys and no file write-back. The FTS sync is also skipped for from-disk? (db_listener.cljs:36). The UI's invoke-hooks (modules/outliner/pipeline.cljs:56-59) then d/transact!s the tx into the UI's DataScript copy and calls ui-handler/re-render-root! (ui.cljs:81-93: clear-query-state! plus request-render of every query component and the root). While parsing, the main area is the progress view (components/container.cljs:156-163), which subscribes to :graph/parsing-state and therefore updates without re-render-root!.

WATCHER: handle-add-and-change! (fs/watcher_handler.cljs:43-62) calls alter-file with {:re-render-root? true :from-disk? true :fs/event :fs/local-file-change} (watcher_handler.cljs:57). That is the same reset-file path, so today it stores per change and re-renders twice (the pipeline plus file.cljs:173). The startup reconcile load-graph-files! (watcher_handler.cljs:136) runs from :graph/ready (events.cljs:172-188, fired by :graph/restored at events.cljs:260-265). It string-compares every file and sends each differing or missing file through handle-changed! (watcher_handler.cljs:192), which is the same per-file, non-bulk path.

changes.change:
For file graphs, honour a deferred store only when the bulk loader asks for it. This works around the fork stripping :skip-store? (conn.cljc:104) and mirrors the DB-graph branch without validation. Sketch:
(and (not db-based?) (:bulk-load? tx-meta))
(let [tx-report (d/with db tx-data (assoc tx-meta :skip-store? true))]
  (when (seq (:tx-data tx-report))
    (reset! conn (:db-after tx-report))
    (dc/store-after-transact! conn tx-report)   ; only appends to :tx-tail, no SQLite write
    (dc/run-callbacks conn (update tx-report :tx-meta dissoc :skip-store?)))
  tx-report)
The key is deliberately :bulk-load?, not :skip-store?, so every other file-graph transact (including thread-api/transact) keeps storing each time, as today.

design.ui_contract_risks:
- Watcher, external edits and the startup reconcile (watcher_handler.cljs:57, 136-205) never set :bulk-load?. They keep the d/transact! path, storing every change, and keep both re-renders. They need them: for from-disk? the worker skips invoke-hooks-default (worker/pipeline.cljs:517-518), so there are no affected-keys and re-render-root! is the UI's only refresh.
- Other file-graph transacts (thread-api/transact from the UI, validate-existing-file's rename transact at reset.cljs:~38, create-today-journal, gc's transact) are unchanged and still store. During a bulk parse, any one of them writes everything pending (tail overflow, then store-impl!). That is a consistent, unplanned checkpoint, not a bug.
- DB graphs: the new branch is guarded by (not db-based?), so the DB-graph branch and its validation are untouched.
- The CLI / sqlite_cli.cljs:90 and gp-cli parse-graph don't pass :bulk-load?, so they are unchanged. They could opt in later.
- Stale UI: if the go-loop ended without after-parse, the UI would miss the final render. parse-and-load-file! already catches per-file errors (repo.cljs:106-116), and the flush result is checked, not thrown, so after-parse always runs.
- Message ordering (assumption): the last file's :sync-db-changes is posted with self.postMessage inside the transact (shared_service.cljs:362), before the thread-api replies to reset-file and flush-storage. On the same worker port, delivery is FIFO, so the UI has applied it before after-parse re-renders. If Comlink replies on a different port, :graph/added's redirect-to-home! still re-renders afterwards.
- Progress bar: driven by state/sub [:graph/parsing-state] (container.cljs:156), not by re-render-root!, so it keeps updating.
- Plugins and undo: from-disk transacts never reached :plugin/hook-db-tx (that is only in the :else branch), and the UI conn still receives every tx. Both unchanged.
- :bulk-load? becomes visible in the sync-db-changes tx-meta and in the UI conn's tx-meta; nothing reads it except the new check. :skip-store? is dissoc'd before callbacks.
- Memory: between checkpoints the dirty index nodes and the tail vector stay pinned in the worker. The datom budget keeps this constant.
- thread-api/flush-storage must return nil, or the db value would be transit-serialized.
- Crash / quit mid-parse:
  - SQLite stays consistent. Each checkpoint is one SQLite transaction (db_worker.cljs:151), and WAL is on. The store holds the db exactly as of the last checkpoint, which is a prefix of whole files: each file is one DataScript tx, and the flush writes the entire db value. The ADR's in-place address reuse is committed in the same transaction as the new root, so no mix is visible.
  - The unflushed suffix is lost from SQLite but still exists in markdown.
  - On next launch, the graph is already in the repo list: native_fs.cljs:134-140 runs add-repo! and <export-db without waiting for parsing, because load-new-repo-to-db! returns a core.async channel (repo.cljs:215) that p/do! treats as a value.
  - The app then restores from SQLite (restore.cljs:13), then :graph/restored, then :graph/ready, then load-graph-files! (events.cljs:188). That re-parses every missing or changed file, but through the slow watcher path (per-file store and re-render), and :graph/added (search rebuild) never runs for that graph.
  - The Electron disk copy is only the snapshot taken at parse start: the periodic export skips file graphs (persist_db.cljs:59, 76-79). This behaviour is the same today; the change only moves the checkpoint granularity from per file to per budget.
design.expected_gain:
Measured: the per-file gap between parses (finished → next start) has a median of 96 ms at g-10k (1159 s = 19.3 min total, flat across 2000-file buckets) and 141 ms at g-real (87.9 s of 97 s). mldoc parse is about 8 %.

This change removes two per-file costs from that gap:
- the SQLite write: store-tail on every file, plus a store-impl! rewriting the dirty leaves and ancestors of three indexes every few files. A leaf touched by hundreds of files is now serialized once per checkpoint.
- the whole-root re-render with query-state reset on the UI thread, which the loop waits on through the promise chain.

The split of the 96 ms between store, extract/build-file-tx, transit plus the UI transact, re-render and the round trip has NOT been measured, so I can't give a number yet. Add LSPERF timers around transact, store and the UI hook first. If store and re-render are the bulk of it, first open should drop by more than half.

What stays linear in file count (first open is inherently O(files); the aim is a smaller constant and bounded stalls):
- mldoc parse, extract, build-file-tx and the worker DataScript transact
- the per-file thread-api round trip (still one file in flight)
- transit of every tx to the UI, and the UI's d/transact! into its copy
- checkpoint writes, amortized O(total datoms), now in budget-sized chunks

The largest single worker stall on this path becomes max(checkpoint, final flush), bounded by the datom budget rather than graph size.

Fuller ADR-003 version:
- (a) Resumable bulk load: write a :logseq.kv/bulk-load-state {:status :in-progress :done n :generation g} datom in the bulk transact just before each checkpoint, so it persists atomically with the data. On the next open, resume the bulk loader (mtime+size reconcile, bulk mode, then the :graph/added work such as the search rebuild) instead of the per-file watcher path.
- (b) load-graph-files! switches to bulk mode above its existing 100-file threshold.
- (c) Don't ship bulk tx-data to the UI at all; after the flush the UI fetches bounded initial data, as on reopen. This also cuts renderer memory (949 MB at 10k).
- (d) Several files per thread-api call and/or the parse-worker (parallel_load.cljs) to remove the one-in-flight round trip.

design.open_questions:
1. The 96 ms/file gap has not been broken down (store vs extract/build-tx vs UI transit, transact and re-render vs round trip). Add LSPERF timers first, or together with the change, to confirm the gain.
2. Upstream's `:skip-store?` on thread-api/transact ("delay writes to the disk", db_worker.cljs:600-603) does nothing for file graphs because of the fork's -transact!. Whether to honour it generally is a separate decision. Honouring it would need an idle or periodic flush, since only a later non-skip transact ever persists a deferred tail, and quitting would drop it. Markdown plus load-graph-files! reconcile would recover it, but slowly.
3. The checkpoint budget (I suggest starting around 50k datoms) needs measuring: stall vs datoms per checkpoint.
4. Assumption: sync-db-changes and the Comlink reply share the worker port, so ordering is FIFO. It isn't verified in browser.cljs; :graph/added's redirect-to-home! is the fallback re-render.
5. After a mid-parse crash the reconcile is correct but runs the slow per-file watcher path, and :graph/added (search rebuild) never runs for that graph. The resumable bulk-load marker (fuller version) fixes both.
6. native_fs.cljs:134-140 runs add-repo!, <export-db and set-loading-files! at the START of the parse, because p/do! treats the graph-added channel as a value. Probably unintended. Awaiting it would make the Electron disk copy a complete graph; decide separately.
7. Related to the empty blocks_fts at 10k (not this task): from-disk? transacts skip the incremental FTS sync (db_listener.cljs:36). So external edits and reconcile never update the block search index; only :graph/added's full rebuild does.

critique.citation_errors:
Most file:line citations hold: db.cljs:105/127/138, conn.cljc:29/90/104/111, storage.cljs:77/91/141/144, graph_parser.cljs:187, repo.cljs:91/146/147/155/178/214/215/223, file.cljs:36/139/154/208, both pipelines at :56 and :517, db_worker.cljs:256/603/825-829, and the events, watcher_handler, native_fs, persist_db and sqlite_cli refs. Wrong or misleading:
(1) "The split of the 96 ms ... has NOT been measured." Partly false. ~/.cache/lsbench/out-10k/open-console.log already holds 7491 LSPERF entries for thread-api/reset-file with worker sync-ms over 50 ms: median 102, p99 386, max 689, sum 937 s. Per 1000-file bucket the mean rises from 116 to 132 ms. So at least 937 s of the ~1250 s parse wall time (parse 91.5 s + gap 1159 s) is synchronous worker time inside reset-file. The UI side (two transit reads, the UI transact, re-render, round trip) is at most ~20-25 ms per file.
(2) The message-ordering argument ("On the same worker port, delivery is FIFO, so the UI has applied it before after-parse re-renders"): the UI does not apply :sync-db-changes when the message arrives. handler/worker.cljs:45-46 re-publishes it with state/pub-event! (state.cljs:1201-1207, async/put!). The events go-loop (events.cljs:432-451) later runs events.cljs:406-412 → pipeline/invoke-hooks. Port FIFO therefore does not imply "applied". It is practically safe only because of the extra flush round trip.
(3) "tx-meta reaches the UI unchanged except :skip-store? (db_listener.cljs:28-34)": the dissoc happens at conn.cljc:104, not in db_listener.
(4) "Unstored nodes have no address": wrong for this persistent-sorted-set fork (org.clojars.tiensonqin/persistent-sorted-set 0.1.2). Modified nodes keep their old _address and are marked dirty: new-node … _address in node-conj, and Leaf store-aux stores when `(or _dirty (nil? _address))`. Dirtiness, not a missing address, is what pins them.
(5) Minor: upsert-addr-content! starts at db_worker.cljs:146; restore.cljs is src/main/frontend/db/restore.cljs:13.
critique.breakages:
(A) The claim "checkpoint stall bounded by the datom budget rather than graph size" does not hold, and at 10k it probably gets worse than today.
- In file graphs `:block/title {:db/index true}` (deps/db/src/logseq/db/file_based/schema.cljs:79), and blocks keep their full content there (`:block/title content`, graph_parser/block.cljs:610). So the AVET :block/title leaves hold the whole block text, sorted by value, and new blocks land spread across all of them. Block uuids are squuids (extract.cljc:343), so :block/uuid AVET is mostly append-only; title is the bad attribute.
- A 50k-datom checkpoint is roughly 4k new blocks. Leaves are capped at 512 entries, so g-10k has only a few hundred title leaves, and one checkpoint dirties almost all of them and re-serializes nearly all block text in the graph (tens of MB of transit plus the SQLite upsert).
- So each checkpoint stall grows linearly with graph size and can be several seconds at 10k, against today's max of 598 ms per 1 s window. Total checkpoint work is (N/B)·O(graph), which is quadratic until the leaf count far exceeds B divided by datoms per block.
- A smaller B does not fix this: each new title costs about one full leaf rewrite. Bounded stalls and low write amplification pull against each other while title stays in AVET, and AVET title has readers (initial_data.cljs:29, reference.cljs:133, embedding.cljs:197).
(B) Unplanned checkpoints get large. Any non-bulk transact during a refresh or re-index (the watcher is live from an earlier :graph/added, thread-api/transact from the UI, the rename transact in validate-existing-file) now writes the whole pending tail through store-impl!. Under (A) that is a surprise stall of whole-index size.
(C) No functional breakage found:
- Leaf and node splits give the second half a nil address (PSS node-conj and Leaf node-conj), so two nodes never share an address.
- new-sqlite-storage ignores delete-addrs, so no deferred deletes can go wrong.
- DB graphs are guarded.
- The node-test path has no storage.
- No existing tests reference skip-store, store-after-transact or transact-sync (grep of src/test and deps/*/test).
critique.gain_doubts:
- The measured data (out-10k/open-console.log) shows the per-file cost is almost all synchronous worker time in reset-file: 102-132 ms per call, growing slowly over the run. Skipping re-render-root! can therefore save at most ~20% of the gap, and probably much less. The UI still does two transit reads and its own d/transact! per file, and rum renders on the next frame, overlapping the worker's next file.
- How much of the ~95 ms non-parse worker time is store-tail/store-impl!, versus extract, build-file-tx, get-blocks-to-delete/validate, the DataScript transact and the listener transit, is still unmeasured. So "more than half" is a guess.
- The AVET-title write amplification in (A) suggests store is a large share today, which supports a real total gain. But the gain arrives as fewer, much bigger stalls, which conflicts with ADR-003's "never choke".
- reset-file also transit-serializes the whole tx back to the UI (reset.cljs returns `(:tx …)`), on top of :sync-db-changes. The loop only uses it to find the page name (repo.cljs:185-191). That duplicate stays and is not addressed.

design.item: gc-on-open: move GC + VACUUM off the graph open path (db worker)
design.summary: Today `<create-or-open-db!` runs `gc-sqlite-dbs!` synchronously before it resolves, and the renderer waits for that before it asks for `get-initial-data`. On a new graph (no stamp), and on any open more than 3 days after the last GC, the open therefore pays for a full scan of the `kvs` table, the deletes and a VACUUM of both the main and client-ops dbs. That was measured at 1.4–1.8 s even on the near-empty demo db. The smallest fix: on open, only check whether GC is due (a cheap kv lookup). If it is, arm a per-repo worker timer that runs the same GC later, once no transaction has happened for a while, behind guards that confirm the same db, conn and pool are still open.
design.current_behavior:
**What GC does** (src/main/frontend/worker/db_worker.cljs:310-323, `gc-sqlite-dbs!`):
- It reads `:logseq.kv/graph-last-gc-at` from the DataScript conn (line 313).
- It runs when `full-gc?` is set, the stamp is nil or not a number, or the stamp is older than 3 days (314-317).
- For the main db, and the client-ops db unless publishing (319), it calls `sqlite-gc/gc-kvs-table!` and then `.exec db "VACUUM"` (320-321).
- Finally it stamps the time with `ldb/transact!` (322-323).

**What `gc-kvs-table!` does** (deps/db/src/logseq/db/sqlite/gc.cljs:43-57):
- One SQL pass: every row whose `addr` appears in no row's `addresses` JSON (`json_each` over the whole table plus `NOT IN`, gc.cljs:18-25), minus addr 0, addr 1 and the three index roots (36).
- It deletes those rows in one `.transaction` (51-54). A normal run removes one layer of orphans; with `:full-gc?` it repeats until nothing is left (55-56).

**What it protects against**: disk growth only, not correctness.
- The worker's `IStorage` `-store` ignores the delete list it receives (db_worker.cljs:240, `_delete-addrs`).
- The DataScript fork collects the addresses of freed B-tree nodes in `*delete-buffer` and hands them to `-store` (storage.cljs:69-72, 119-123 in ~/.gitlibs/libs/datascript/datascript/3971e2d…/src/datascript/).
- So orphaned nodes pile up in `kvs` until GC deletes them, and VACUUM gives the file pages back.

**Callers**:
1. The open path, `(let [r (gc-sqlite-dbs! db client-ops-db conn {})] (perf-phase! "gc") r)` at db_worker.cljs:371 inside `<create-or-open-db!` (325-378).
   - It runs after the conn is restored (352) and `register-transact-pipeline-fn!` (343).
   - It runs before `db-migrate/migrate` (373) and before `db-listener/listen-db-changes!` (378).
2. `:thread-api/gc-graph` (831-837, `{:full-gc? true}`), used only by the dev shortcut `:dev/gc-graph` → `repo-handler/gc-graph!` (src/main/frontend/handler/repo.cljs:232-238).

**Why it blocks the open**:
- `<create-or-open-db!` is reached via `start-db!` (475-484) from `:thread-api/create-or-open-db` (486-490) and `on-become-master` (~955-960).
- The renderer's `<fetch-initial-data` awaits `create-or-open-db` and only then calls `get-initial-data` (src/main/frontend/persist_db/browser.cljs:229-230).
- Every sqlite-wasm call is synchronous in the worker, so the whole GC is one blocking macrotask on the open path.

**Why deferring is safe for the live conn**:
- `:skip-store?` (set by `thread-api/transact`, db_worker.cljs:600-603) is not a timer flush. The fork's `store-after-transact!` just keeps the datoms in the in-memory tail and skips storing (conn.cljc:82-98). The next non-skipped transact writes the tail, or runs `store-impl!` when the tail overflows.
- At any moment the in-memory current tree references only (a) nodes reachable from the stored root, or (b) dirty nodes that have not been stored yet.
- GC deletes only rows that no row references, so it cannot delete anything the current conn needs, whatever the pending tail holds.
- Today's open path already runs VACUUM while a restored conn is live (the conn is created at line 352), so VACUUM does not break live address references.

**About the measured "gc (skipped)" phase**:
- The 0–101 ms reopen number is not GC. That `perf-phase!` record covers everything since "schema-fix": restoring the client-ops conn (355), the `initial-data-exists?` check, and the GC due-check.
- GC's own size-dependence on big dbs has not been measured.

**Instrumentation**:
- The only instrumented GC line is db_worker.cljs:371.
- bench/instrumentation.patch:164-165 replays that same line.
- bench/lssummary.js does not refer to the "gc" phase name (grep found none).
- The thread-api perf log (thread_api.cljc:52-78) only sees thread-api calls, so a GC run from a timer would be invisible to it without its own `perf-phase!`.

changes.change:
Split the function into a cheap check and the heavy body. Keep `gc-sqlite-dbs!` with the same arity for `:thread-api/gc-graph` (dev full GC, stays synchronous).

```clojure
(def ^:private gc-interval-ms (* 3 24 3600 1000))
(defn- gc-due? [conn]
  (let [t (:kv/value (d/entity @conn :logseq.kv/graph-last-gc-at))]
    (or (not (number? t)) (> (- (common-util/time-ms) t) gc-interval-ms))))
(defn- run-gc! [sqlite-db client-ops-db conn full-gc?]
  (println :debug "gc current graph")
  (doseq [db (if @*publishing? [sqlite-db] [sqlite-db client-ops-db])]
    (sqlite-gc/gc-kvs-table! db {:full-gc? full-gc?})
    (.exec db "VACUUM"))
  (ldb/transact! conn [{:db/ident :logseq.kv/graph-last-gc-at :kv/value (common-util/time-ms)}]))
(defn- gc-sqlite-dbs! [sqlite-db client-ops-db conn {:keys [full-gc?]}]
  (when (or full-gc? (gc-due? conn)) (run-gc! sqlite-db client-ops-db conn full-gc?)))
```

`(not (number? t))` covers nil, so the old `nil?` test is subsumed. The behaviour is otherwise identical.

changes.where: new code placed ABOVE close-db-aux! (i.e. before line 256, e.g. right after new-sqlite-storage), or add (declare cancel-gc-timer!)
changes.change:
Add a per-repo timer, a guard that checks the same db, conn and pool are still open, and a quiet check based on the existing `:db/latest-transact-time`. `sync-db-to-main-thread` sets it on every transaction that passes the listener (db_listener.cljs:22; atom `worker-state/*state`, state.cljs:30, 90-92).

```clojure
(def ^:private gc-first-delay-ms 60000) ; after open
(def ^:private gc-retry-ms 30000)
(def ^:private gc-quiet-ms 30000)      ; no tx for this long
(defonce ^:private *gc-timers (atom {}))
(defn- cancel-gc-timer! [repo]
  (when-let [t (get @*gc-timers repo)] (js/clearTimeout t) (swap! *gc-timers dissoc repo)))
(defn- gc-target-live? [repo db client-ops-db conn]
  (let [{cur-db :db cur-ops :client-ops} (get @*sqlite-conns repo)
        ^js pool (worker-state/get-opfs-pool repo)]
    (and (identical? cur-db db) (identical? cur-ops client-ops-db)
         (identical? (get @*datascript-conns repo) conn)
         (or @*publishing? (and pool (not (.isPaused pool)))))))
(defn- schedule-gc! [repo db client-ops-db conn delay-ms]
  (cancel-gc-timer! repo)
  (swap! *gc-timers assoc repo
    (js/setTimeout
     (fn []
       (swap! *gc-timers dissoc repo)
       (when (and (gc-target-live? repo db client-ops-db conn) (gc-due? conn))
         (let [last-tx (get-in @worker-state/*state [:db/latest-transact-time repo] 0)]
           (if (< (- (common-util/time-ms) last-tx) gc-quiet-ms)
             (schedule-gc! repo db client-ops-db conn gc-retry-ms)
             (try (perf-phase! "gc-deferred-start")
                  (run-gc! db client-ops-db conn false)
                  (perf-phase! "gc-deferred")
                  (catch :default e (log/error ::deferred-gc-failed e)))))))
     delay-ms)))
```

- `run-gc!` does the orphan scan, the delete transaction, VACUUM and the stamp transact all synchronously inside one timer callback, so nothing else in the worker can run in between.
- On error it does not stamp, so the next open schedules again.
- A failed guard drops the job silently. The stamp stays old, so the next open re-arms it.

Replace
`(let [r (gc-sqlite-dbs! db client-ops-db conn {})] (perf-phase! "gc") r)`
with
`(when (gc-due? conn) (schedule-gc! repo db client-ops-db conn gc-first-delay-ms))
 (perf-phase! "gc-check")`

- Renaming the phase makes old and new logs easy to tell apart; lssummary.js does not depend on the name.
- Optionally add `(perf-phase! "client-ops-conn")` right after line 360, so the separate client-ops restore cost is no longer folded into the gc phase.

Add `(cancel-gc-timer! repo)` as the first form. The guard already covers a closed repo; this stops the timer closure from keeping closed db objects alive and ends the retry loop. It covers `close-db!`, `close-other-dbs!` (graph switch via `start-db!`) and `unsafe-unlink-db` (637-642).
Optional: add `(cancel-gc-timer! repo)` before the `gc-sqlite-dbs!` call. Not needed for correctness: the fired timer re-checks `gc-due?`, and after a manual GC the stamp is fresh.

Only VACUUM when it will free something. Before `.exec db "VACUUM"`, read `PRAGMA freelist_count` and `PRAGMA page_count` and skip VACUUM below a threshold (e.g. under 10% free pages). It is not needed for the open-path fix. First measure how the 1.4-1.8 s tiny-db cost splits between the scan and VACUUM, by adding a `perf-phase!` between `gc-kvs-table!` and VACUUM in the instrumented build.
Not product code. Regenerate the patch from the new diff, otherwise re-applying it conflicts on line 371.

design.ui_contract_risks:
- **Renderer open flow** (persist_db/browser.cljs:229-230, handler/repo.cljs): `create-or-open-db` resolves sooner. Its return value (nil) and order of effects are unchanged, except that the gc stamp is no longer written before migrate and listeners.

- **The stamp now goes through the listener.** It is written after `listen-db-changes!` is attached (db_worker.cljs:378), so `sync-db-to-main-thread` (db_listener.cljs:19-44) runs for it:
  - invoke-hooks runs; for file graphs it only syncs pages found in the tx (pipeline.cljs:479-488), and a kv entity is not a page (assumption: `ds-report/get-blocks-and-pages` returns nothing for a `:db/ident`/`:kv/value` entity).
  - It broadcasts one tiny `:sync-db-changes` to the UI.
  - Search sync filters on `:block/uuid`, `:block/name`, `:block/title` and `:block/properties` (search.cljs, `get-affected-blocks`), so nothing is indexed.
  - Nothing in the UI reads `graph-last-gc-at`; grep finds it only in db_worker and kv_entity.
  - If the broadcast is unwanted, pass tx-meta and filter on it, but that is not required.

- **`:thread-api/gc-graph` and `:dev/gc-graph`** (shortcut config.cljs:616-618) keep the same synchronous full-GC behaviour.

- **Other SQLite writers, and why they cannot collide:**
  - All sqlite-wasm OO1 calls are synchronous: the SAH pool uses sync access handles, and `exportFile` is synchronous (sqlite3.mjs:13679-13693). The worker's JS is single-threaded.
  - So a timer-run GC cannot interleave with `upsert-addr-content!` (147-155), `store-tail`, the `export-db` checkpoint plus `exportFile` (654-659), `fix-broken-graph`'s `delete from kvs` (135-139), or `search-upsert-blocks`, which writes a separate search db.
  - `.transaction` takes a synchronous callback, so no SQL transaction is open when the timer fires (VACUUM would fail inside one).
  - Only the shared-service master opens dbs (`start-db!` checks `*master-client?`, 482), and the SAH pool holds exclusive handles, so no other tab or process writes.

- **Changes between arming and firing:**
  - Graph switch or close: `close-db-aux!` cancels the timer; the identity guard is the backstop.
  - `release-access-handles` pauses the pool (647). `pauseVfs` throws if files are open (sqlite3.mjs:13649-13663), so it can only follow a close; `isPaused` (13665-13667) is checked anyway.
  - `unsafe-unlink-db` closes, then removes the VFS.
  - `import-db` (661-666) writes the pool file before open. A re-open creates new db objects, so the old timer's guard fails.
  - `rtc` `full_upload_download_graph` re-opens with `close-other-db? false` (426, 587). Timers are keyed per repo; DB graphs only.

- **Old db values** (the one hazard that GC-on-open never had): a db value captured before a later `store-impl!` and lazily restored after the GC in a later macrotask could hit a deleted address.
  - Inside the worker, `search-blocks` re-derefs `@conn` at each step (search.cljs:359, 385, 402, 408). `build-blocks-indice` and `get-view-data` are synchronous over a single db value.
  - The renderer holds its own DataScript copy, not lazy storage.
  - The quiet window reduces the risk further. ADR-003 decision 3 already treats old db values as non-durable.

- **Mobile**: same worker code, so the same behaviour.

- **Tests**: no existing test references `gc-sqlite-dbs!` or the stamp.
design.expected_gain:
- **Open path**: the whole GC + VACUUM stall leaves the open whenever it is due. Measured: 1568–1796 ms on the first open of the near-empty demo graph with a fresh profile, where a nil stamp means "due"; on large dbs it is larger but not yet measured. Every fresh graph open and every open more than 3 days after the last GC now pays only a `d/entity` kv lookup, which is constant time, plus arming a timer.
- **Normal reopen** (stamp under 3 days old): no change. The reported 0–101 ms "gc" phase was mostly the client-ops conn restore and stays.
- **What stays linear**: the deferred GC itself. The orphan scan is linear in the number of `kvs` rows times their fan-out, VACUUM is linear in the db file size, and both run on the main and client-ops dbs. It still blocks the worker in one macrotask, but at a moment of no transactions at least 60 s after open, not while the user waits for the journals.
- **After first open of g-10k**, the first deferred GC will probably be the largest one, since first open stores once per file and leaves many orphans. It runs only after parsing finishes, because the reset-file transactions keep updating latest-transact-time.
- **Fuller ADR-003 version** (bounded work, not deferred work):
  - Honour `delete-addrs` in `-store`. The fork already collects the addresses of freed nodes (storage.cljs:69-72, 119-123); the worker ignores them at db_worker.cljs:240, and sqlite_cli.cljs:58 must match. Reclaiming becomes proportional to each change, and the full GC becomes a rare consistency check.
  - That needs care on three points:
    - Addresses are reused (storage.cljs:41-47). Delete before upsert in the same transaction, and never delete an address that is in the same upsert batch.
    - Old db values lose freed nodes immediately.
    - It needs a differential test with `sqlite-debug/find-missing-addresses`.
  - Replace full VACUUM with `PRAGMA auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL` (it takes one VACUUM to convert) plus `PRAGMA incremental_vacuum(N)` per idle tick, under a time budget.
  - Schedule on worker quiescence: an in-flight thread-api counter in `remote-function` (thread_api.cljc:52-78) rather than transaction time.
  - A chunked orphan scan would still have to scan everything, since the `json_each` CTE covers the whole table. That is why honouring `delete-addrs` is the real bounded fix.
design.verification:
**Existing tests**
- deps/db/test/logseq/db/sqlite/gc_test.cljs (`^:long`, Node version of the algorithm, unchanged by this design) and the usual frontend and worker test suite, for compile and regressions. No current test exercises the worker GC path.

**New tests**
- Pull the timer decision into a pure function, e.g. `(gc-decision {:live? :due? :now :last-tx})` → `:run`, `:retry` or `:drop`, and unit-test it:
  - nil stamp, a non-number stamp, a 4-day-old stamp and a 1-hour-old stamp;
  - a transaction within the quiet window gives `:retry`;
  - a different db object or a paused pool gives `:drop`.
- Unit-test `gc-due?` against an in-memory conn with and without the kv.

**Harness** (packaged build, LSPERF records)
1. **Fresh profile, demo graph and "Add new graph":** the open-path record is `gc-check` with about 0 ms stall, not 1568–1796 ms. About 60 s after open, and at least 30 s after the last transaction, a `gc-deferred-start` / `gc-deferred` pair appears with the GC stall in `max-lag-ms`. For g-10k first open it must appear only after parsing and the search-index rebuild. `blocks_fts` behaviour is unchanged (a separate issue).
2. **Reopen g-real and g-10k with an old stamp** (make the kv older than 3 days, e.g. with a temporary dev override of `gc-interval-ms` or by setting the stamp on a graph copy): the open-path phases match the skipped case. Record the `gc-deferred` stall at both sizes. This is the first measurement of how GC scales with graph size, which ADR-003 plan step 1 asked for.
3. **Integrity:** after a deferred GC, export the db (the `export-db` thread-api) and run `sqlite-debug/find-missing-addresses` on it: expect no missing addresses. Reopen the graph and check journals, search and a page open.
4. **Lifecycle:** switch graphs within 60 s of opening. There must be no worker error, and no `gc-deferred` record for the old repo. Repeat with a window reload (`release-access-handles`) and with removing a graph.
5. **Check the stamp:** after a deferred GC, the next reopen logs `gc-check` without a deferred run.
design.open_questions:
- **Constants**: the 60 s first delay, 30 s quiet window and 30 s retry are guesses. The quiet check uses transaction time only, so a deferred GC can overlap read-heavy work or search db writes such as the FTS rebuild round-trips. That is safe (synchronous calls, a different db file) but can stack stalls. An in-flight thread-api counter in thread_api.cljc `remote-function` would fix that, at the cost of touching the file that also holds the perf instrumentation.
- **Tiny-db cost split**: unknown whether the 1.4–1.8 s on a tiny db is mostly VACUUM on OPFS SAH-pool (a fixed cost) or the scan. That decides whether gating VACUUM on the freelist is worth it.
- **Deferred GC size at 10k**: unmeasured. If it stalls for several seconds even when idle, that argues for moving on to `delete-addrs` plus incremental vacuum.
- **Why upstream ignores `delete-addrs`** in `-store`: unknown; possibly because of old db values or the address-reuse edge case. This needs checking before the fuller version.
- **Assumption**: `ds-report/get-blocks-and-pages` finds no page in the kv-only stamp transaction, so no markdown write is triggered. I did not read that function; confirm, or give the stamp tx-meta that invoke-hooks ignores.
- **Assumption**: every file graph's SQLite db was created by this code base, so a nil stamp means a new db. With the deferral a nil stamp still leads to a deferred GC, not a skip. That is deliberate: first open leaves many orphans behind.

design.summary: At 10k journals the block index is not lost to a size limit or a thrown error. The rebuild is a fire-and-forget chain that the UI thread drives, one step at a time (pages, truncate, worker build, UI transform, worker upsert). It starts once, at :graph/added. It keeps no progress and nothing restarts it on reopen. At 10k the worker never ran the build step before the app closed: the renderer was busy, and the harness's "quiet" check cannot see a busy UI thread. Fix: move the whole rebuild into the worker as a batched walk over the :block/uuid index with a cursor. Each batch commits in its own transaction together with a progress row in the search db; the walk yields between batches and resumes on open. The UI only triggers it.

changes.change:
1) Progress table. Add `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS search_meta (k TEXT PRIMARY KEY, v TEXT)` to create-tables-and-triggers!. drop-tables-and-triggers! must not drop it. Before creating, check `select 1 from sqlite_master where name='blocks'`:

Add helpers `(get-meta db k)` and `(set-meta-tx! tx k v)` (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(k) DO UPDATE SET v=excluded.v).

2) Batch walker, `index-batch [db cursor {:keys [max-items max-ms]}]`:
```clojure
(let [t0 (js/performance.now)
      ds (if cursor
           (drop-while #(= cursor (:v %)) (d/index-range db :block/uuid cursor nil))
           (d/datoms db :avet :block/uuid))]
  (loop [ds ds rows (transient []) n 0 last nil]
    (if-let [dt (first ds)]
      (if (or (>= n max-items) (> (- (js/performance.now) t0) max-ms))
        {:rows (persistent! rows) :last last :done? false}
        (let [e (d/entity db (:e dt))
              row (when-not (hidden-entity? e) (block->index e))]
          (recur (rest ds) (cond-> rows row (conj! row)) (inc n) (:v dt))))
      {:rows (persistent! rows) :last last :done? true})))
```
:block/uuid is unique, so it is AVET-indexed (file_based/schema.cljs:16); index-range is already used at embedding.cljs:74. Looking up the entity by :e avoids get-all-blocks' second lookup by uuid.

3) Commit, `commit-batch! [search-db rows state cursor]`: one `.transaction` that upserts rows with the same SQL as upsert-blocks!, but SKIPS (with a console.warn and a count) any row whose id or page fails uuid-string?, instead of throwing. In the same transaction, set blocks_state and blocks_cursor (`(str cursor)`). Progress and rows are therefore crash-consistent. Consider applying the same skip-don't-throw rule to upsert-blocks! (119-133), which the incremental path uses.

4) The rebuild must not build the Fuse page index. On completion, do `(swap! fuzzy-search-indices dissoc repo)`; it is rebuilt lazily on the next search (290-307, lines 301-302) and skipped above 2500 pages anyway.
